source: Caltrain (Peninsula Corridor JPB): "FY2026 Annual Ridership Report" presentation to the JPB Board, October 1, 2026; and "Caltrain Ridership Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Report" (Caltrain Planning, September 2025)
period: Fiscal Year 2026 = July 2025 - June 2026 (primary); FY2025 = July 2024 - June 2025; 2019 = pre-COVID annual passenger count (winter 2019)

systemwide.avgWeekdayRidershipFY2026_note: Published rounded ("FY2026 Average Weekday Ridership was 40,800"). All weekdays (Mon-Fri), systemwide, unlinked boardings.

amwrByCountyFY2025.note: FY2025 report Table 4. The SF county figure 8,303 = San Francisco 6,874 + 22nd Street 1,261 + Bayshore 168, i.e. Caltrain counts Bayshore (physically in Brisbane, San Mateo County) under San Francisco. 2019 equivalents: SF 17,159; total 63,606.

notes: Station figures are AMWR = Average Mid-Week Ridership (Tuesday-Thursday) by ORIGIN station, i.e. boardings, not alightings. Caltrain says the fare model cannot yet estimate destination stations. Mid-week is ~20% above Mon/Fri in FY2026 (presentation p.9), so AMWR overstates an all-weekday average; systemwide AWR (all weekdays) is 40,800 vs sum of station AMWR 44262 (sum computed here).

Method: Caltrain has no fare gates or APCs (yet); FY2025/FY2026 numbers are model estimates from the Fare Media Sales-Based Ridership Estimation Model (ticket and pass sales, with assumed trips per pass: monthly pass = 37 trips/month from Jan 2025). Does not count fare evasion. NTD-reported ridership has historically been higher than this model.
The annual passenger count (full on-board census) was discontinued in 2020; 2019 values are from the 2019 Annual Passenger Count (pre-COVID, secondary only).
"San Francisco" station = 4th & King. inSanFranciscoCity marks San Francisco and 22nd Street; Bayshore is just south of the city line in Brisbane but is grouped with SF county by Caltrain.

The full written FY2026 Annual Ridership Report was not yet posted when accessed (the presentation says it is "to be posted on the ridership webpage"); figures here come from the board presentation, which matches the 2026-09-30 press release (SF station 9,714; AWR 40,800).

Most recent monthly: Executive Director report (JPB board, 2026-09-03) says July 2026 weekday ridership +18.7% vs July 2025 and 67.3% of 2019 (weekday); a chart label of 1,321,627 total riders, consistent with the press-release figure of 1.32 million for July 2026. The July 2026 AWR value is only in a chart and was not extractable.
